analysis: The code snippet defines a method JSON2HTML that takes a String name. Before any substring calls, there is a check: if (name.length() < 1) return name; This ensures that if name is not null, its length is at least 1 for all subsequent code. The substring API declares IndexOutOfBoundsException when beginIndex is negative or larger than the length of the string. In the code, substring is called with beginIndex 0 and 1. For beginIndex=0, it is always valid (0 <= length >= 1). For beginIndex=1, it is valid when length >= 1, which holds because of the early return. Additionally, the substring(1) is called on the result of name.replace("_", " "), which has the same length as name (replace does not change length when no underscore, and replacing underscore with space keeps length the same). Thus every substring invocation satisfies the preconditions. No NullPointerException is considered because the question focuses on exceptions declared by substring.
remark: The early length check (name.length() < 1) ensures that all subsequent substring calls operate on strings of length at least 1. Substring(0) is always safe for nonempty strings. Substring(1) is safe because if length == 1, beginIndex=1 is equal to length and allowed; if length > 1, also safe. The replace method does not alter string length, so the secondary substring(1) is similarly safe. Therefore, no trigger scenario for IndexOutOfBoundsException exists in the given code context.
